title: Colour grade
description: A display-referred colour grade (look uplift L2, GH-943, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-look-uplift-design.md section 3). The renderer bakes it into a 32x32x32 3D LUT at boot and folds a lookup into OutputPass, after the tone map and the sRGB encode and before the vignette. App-read only: the sim never sees a grade. EVERY colour is a PALETTE KEY ('ramp.index', 'reserved.name'), never a raw hex: a key's HUE DIRECTION (its colour minus its own luma, scaled so the largest channel is 1) is what is applied, and the sibling `amount` says how hard. Order of operations: warmth, then lift/gamma/gain, then saturation, then split tone. The identity values (lift level 0 and amount 0, gamma value 1 and amount 0, gain value 1 and amount 0, saturation 1, warmth 0, split-tone amounts 0) build NO pass. Day is the identity grade and ships no file. `pnpm validate:data` checks every key resolves to a palette entry.

id.description: Also the filename, and what `&grade=` and a mission's `map.grade` name.

lift.description: Added in the shadows, fading to nothing at white: out = lift * (1 - c) + gain * c.

amount.description: How much of the tint's hue direction is added to the black point, in encoded 0..1 units.

level.description: A neutral lift of the black point.

gamma.description: The mid-tone curve: out = v ^ (1 / gamma). Above 1 brightens the mids.

amount.description: A per-channel gamma skew along the tint's hue direction.
A per-channel gain skew along the tint's hue direction.

saturation.description: 1 is unchanged. Scales each colour's distance from its own Rec.709 luma.

warmth.description: A white-balance shift: positive raises red and lowers blue.

balance.description: Slides the crossover: negative gives the shadow tint more of the frame.

paletteKey.description: A palette key such as 'water.1' or 'dust.0'. Never a raw hex. Keep to the ramps: the reserved vfx and team bands are runtime-only.

amount.description: How much of the tint's hue direction is added, in encoded 0..1 units.
